title: OBLIGATION
notes:
✓ Obligation → something that you must do because it is necessary, required, expected, or a rule.

✓ You must wear a uniform.
✓ Students have to attend classes.
✓ You should respect the rules.

◆ MAIN EXPRESSIONS
must, have to, have got to, need to, should, ought to, be required to.

title: MUST
notes:
✓ Must → expresses strong obligation, necessity, or a rule imposed by the speaker/authority.

✓ You must finish your homework today.
✓ Visitors must show identification.
✓ You must follow the safety rules.

✓ Must is especially common for strong personal or official requirements.

◆ PATTERN
subject + must + base verb.

⚠️ After must, use the base form of the verb.
❌ You must to study.
✓ You must study.

title: HAVE TO
notes:
✓ Have to → expresses necessity or obligation, often because of an external rule, situation, or requirement.

✓ I have to go to school every day.
✓ We have to submit the application by Friday.
✓ She has to wear a uniform.

◆ PRESENT
I/you/we/they → have to
He/she/it → has to

◆ PAST
had to
✓ I had to leave early.

◆ FUTURE
will have to
✓ We will have to wait.

title: MUST VS HAVE TO
notes:
✓ Both express strong obligation, but the source of the obligation can differ.

◆ MUST → obligation strongly felt or stated by the speaker.
✓ You must be careful.

◆ HAVE TO → obligation caused by an external rule, situation, or requirement.
✓ I have to wear a uniform at school.

✓ In everyday English, have to is very common and often replaces must.

⚠️ The distinction is not absolute; context determines the meaning.

title: MUSTN'T
notes:
✓ Mustn't / must not → prohibition; something is not allowed.

✓ You mustn't smoke here.
✓ Students mustn't use phones during the exam.
✓ You must not enter this room.

✓ MUSTN'T = prohibited.

⚠️ Do not confuse mustn't with don't have to.

✓ You mustn't leave. → You are not allowed to leave.
✓ You don't have to leave. → It is not necessary to leave.

title: DON'T HAVE TO
notes:
✓ Don't/doesn't have to → absence of necessity; something is optional.

✓ You don't have to come early.
✓ She doesn't have to wear a uniform today.
✓ We don't have to pay now.

✓ DON'T HAVE TO = no obligation.

⚠️ It does NOT mean prohibition.

✓ You don't have to attend. → You may attend or not.
✓ You mustn't attend. → You are not allowed to attend.

title: NEED TO
notes:
✓ Need to → expresses necessity or something that is necessary to do.

✓ I need to study for the exam.
✓ You need to submit the form.
✓ She needs to get some rest.

◆ PATTERN
subject + need(s) to + base verb.

✓ I need to work.
✓ He needs to work.

✓ Need to is common in everyday English and is often less forceful than must.

title: NEEDN'T
notes:
✓ Needn't → it is not necessary to do something.

✓ You needn't bring anything.
✓ We needn't hurry.
✓ She needn't worry.

✓ Needn't = there is no necessity.

✓ You needn't come tomorrow.
= You don't have to come tomorrow.

⚠️ Needn't is followed directly by the base verb.

❌ You needn't to come.
✓ You needn't come.

title: HAVE GOT TO
notes:
✓ Have got to → expresses strong necessity or obligation, especially in informal speech.

✓ I've got to go now.
✓ You've got to finish this today.
✓ She's got to study harder.

✓ Meaning is generally similar to have to.

✓ I have to leave.
= I've got to leave.

⚠️ It is mainly used for present situations and is more conversational.

title: SHOULD
notes:
✓ Should → expresses advice, recommendation, or a weaker sense of obligation.

✓ You should study regularly.
✓ We should respect our teachers.
✓ You should arrive on time.

✓ Should is weaker than must/have to.

✓ You must wear a helmet. → strong requirement.
✓ You should wear a helmet. → advice/recommendation.

title: OUGHT TO
notes:
✓ Ought to → expresses duty, advice, or what is considered the right thing to do.

✓ You ought to respect your parents.
✓ We ought to help people in need.
✓ You ought to apologize.

◆ PATTERN
ought to + base verb.

✓ Ought to is similar to should but is somewhat more formal and less common in everyday speech.

title: BE REQUIRED TO
notes:
✓ Be required to → expresses an official rule, law, regulation, or formal requirement.

✓ Students are required to wear uniforms.
✓ Applicants are required to provide identification.
✓ Employees are required to follow safety procedures.

✓ Common in formal, academic, workplace, and official contexts.

◆ PATTERN
be + required + to + base verb.

title: BE SUPPOSED TO
notes:
✓ Be supposed to → expresses an expected duty, rule, arrangement, or responsibility.

✓ Students are supposed to arrive on time.
✓ You are supposed to submit the assignment today.
✓ We are supposed to meet at 5 p.m.

✓ Meaning → what someone is expected or instructed to do.

⚠️ It can describe expectations rather than a strict legal requirement.

title: OBLIGATION IN DIFFERENT TIMES
notes:
◆ PRESENT
✓ I must study.
✓ I have to study.
✓ I need to study.

◆ PAST
✓ I had to study.
✓ I needed to study.

⚠️ For a completed past obligation, use had to rather than must in ordinary statements.

✓ I had to leave early yesterday.

◆ FUTURE
✓ I will have to study tomorrow.
✓ I will need to study tomorrow.

✓ Have to is especially useful because it can easily express past and future obligation.

title: QUESTIONS ABOUT OBLIGATION
notes:
✓ Ask about obligation using Do/Does/Did + subject + have to...?

✓ Do I have to attend?
✓ Does she have to wear a uniform?
✓ Did you have to pay?

✓ Must can also be used in questions, especially for formal or speaker-imposed requirements.

✓ Must I finish this today?

✓ In everyday English, 'Do I have to...?' is usually more natural.

title: NEGATIVE OBLIGATION
notes:
✓ There are two important negative meanings:

◆ MUSTN'T → prohibition.
✓ You mustn't park here.
= Parking is not allowed.

◆ DON'T HAVE TO → no necessity.
✓ You don't have to park here.
= Parking here is not necessary.

◆ NEEDN'T → no necessity.
✓ You needn't bring your passport.
= It is unnecessary.

✓ KEY DIFFERENCE:
MUSTN'T = NOT ALLOWED.
DON'T HAVE TO / NEEDN'T = NOT NECESSARY.

title: OBLIGATION STRENGTH
notes:
✓ MUST → very strong obligation.
✓ HAVE TO → strong/necessary obligation.
✓ BE REQUIRED TO → official/formal requirement.
✓ HAVE GOT TO → strong, conversational obligation.
✓ NEED TO → necessary action.
✓ SHOULD → advice or weaker duty.
✓ OUGHT TO → advice/duty.
✓ BE SUPPOSED TO → expected responsibility.

✓ Choose the expression according to the strength and source of the obligation.

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ You must to study.
✓ You must study.

❌ He musts study.
✓ He must study.

❌ She have to leave.
✓ She has to leave.

❌ You don't must go.
✓ You mustn't go. → prohibition.
✓ You don't have to go. → no necessity.

❌ You mustn't come if you don't want to.
→ This means you are prohibited from coming.

✓ You don't have to come if you don't want to.
→ Coming is optional.

❌ I musted leave yesterday.
✓ I had to leave yesterday.

❌ You needn't to worry.
✓ You needn't worry.

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. Strong rule/obligation → must / have to.

◆ 2. External requirement → have to / be required to.

◆ 3. Official requirement → be required to.

◆ 4. Strong informal necessity → have got to.

◆ 5. General necessity → need to.

◆ 6. Advice or weaker duty → should / ought to.

◆ 7. Expected responsibility → be supposed to.

◆ 8. Prohibition → mustn't.

◆ 9. No necessity → don't have to / needn't.

◆ 10. Past obligation → had to.

◆ 11. Future obligation → will have to.

✓ Golden rule → MUSTN'T means 'not allowed'; DON'T HAVE TO and NEEDN'T mean 'not necessary.'
